entities.summary:
John William Cheever was an American short story writer and novelist. He is sometimes called "the Chekhov of the suburbs". His fiction is mostly set on the Upper East Side of Manhattan; the Westchester suburbs; old New England villages based on various South Shore towns around Quincy, Massachusetts, where he was born; and Italy, especially Rome. His short stories included "The Enormous Radio", "Goodbye, My Brother", "The Five-Forty-Eight", "The Country Husband", and "The Swimmer", and he also wrote five novels: The Wapshot Chronicle ,
The Wapshot Scandal, Bullet Park (1969), Falconer (1977) and a novella, Oh What a Paradise It Seems (1982).

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: John Cheever's works are notable for their portrayal of suburban American life in the mid-20th century, influencing literary movements such as the New England School and contributing to a nuanced understanding of the human condition. His writing has been widely studied and anthologized, with many of his stories continuing to be taught in high school English classes.
